name: Apollo 11 Landing Site (Tranquility Base)
notes: Lunar Module (LM) Eagle descent stage in Mare Tranquillitatis. Coordinate system: Mean Earth/Polar Axis, latitude [-90..90] (south negative), longitude [-180..180] (east positive). Precision coordinates derived from LROC NAC imaging (Wagner et al., 2017).

name: Apollo 12 Landing Site (Ocean of Storms)
notes: LM Intrepid descent stage in Oceanus Procellarum, landed 160 m from Surveyor 3. Longitude in -180..180 deg E system (-23.4219 deg E = 23.4219 deg W; 336.5781 deg E in 0..360 system).

name: Apollo 14 Landing Site (Fra Mauro)
notes: LM Antares descent stage in Fra Mauro formation. Longitude in -180..180 deg E system (-17.47194 deg E = 17.47194 deg W; 342.52806 deg E in 0..360 system).

name: Apollo 15 Landing Site (Hadley-Apennine)
notes: LM Falcon descent stage near Hadley Rille and Montes Apenninus. Longitude in -180..180 deg E system.

name: Apollo 16 Landing Site (Descartes)
notes: LM Orion descent stage in Descartes Highlands. Longitude in -180..180 deg E system.

name: Apollo 17 Landing Site (Taurus-Littrow)
notes: LM Challenger descent stage in Taurus-Littrow valley. Longitude in -180..180 deg E system.

name: Chandrayaan-3 Landing Site (Statio Shiv Shakti)
notes: Vikram lander touchdown point between Manzinus C and Simpelius N craters. Officially approved by IAU as Statio Shiv Shakti on 2024-03-19 (69.373 deg S, 32.319 deg E). ISRO operational estimates reported ~69.37 deg S, 32.35 deg E.

name: Chang'e 3 Landing Site (Statio Tianhe)
notes: Landed in northern Mare Imbrium. Officially named Statio Tianhe by IAU. Longitude in -180..180 deg E system (-19.5116 deg E = 19.5116 deg W; 340.4884 deg E in 0..360 system).

name: Chang'e 4 Landing Site (Statio Tianhe / Von Karman)
notes: First landing on lunar farside, inside Von Karman crater (South Pole-Aitken basin). Officially named Statio Tianhe by IAU. LROC Narrow Angle Camera confirmed coordinates: 45.457 deg S, 177.589 deg E.

name: Chang'e 5 Landing Site (Statio Tianchuan)
notes: Lunar sample return mission in northern Oceanus Procellarum near Mons Rumker. Officially named Statio Tianchuan by IAU. Longitude in -180..180 deg E system (-51.9161 deg E = 51.9161 deg W; 308.0839 deg E in 0..360 system).

name: Chang'e 6 Landing Site (Apollo Basin)
notes: First lunar farside sample return touchdown in southern Apollo impact basin. Documented in Nature Geoscience (2024) and verified by LROC NAC at 41.6385 deg S, 206.0148 deg E (-153.9852 deg E in -180..180 system).

name: SLIM Landing Site (Shioli Crater)
notes: Smart Lander for Investigating Moon (SLIM). Achieved pinpoint landing within 55 m of target on the slope of Shioli crater. Confirmed by JAXA and LROC imaging at 13.3160 deg S, 25.2510 deg E (elevation -912 m).

name: Intuitive Machines IM-1 Odysseus Landing Site (Malapert A)
notes: First commercial soft landing under NASA Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS). Odysseus lander touched down near Malapert A crater at 80.13 deg S, 1.44 deg E (elevation 2579 m). Peer-reviewed 55th LPSC documentation.

name: Intuitive Machines IM-2 Athena Landing Site (Mons Mouton)
notes: NASA CLPS delivery carrying PRIME-1 drill and mass spectrometer to prospect for water ice. Targeted on the elevated plateau of Mons Mouton at 84.79 deg S, 29.20 deg E.

name: Firefly Blue Ghost Mission 1 Landing Site (Mare Crisium)
notes: NASA CLPS delivery TO19D delivering 10 NASA science payloads to Mare Crisium near Mons Latreille volcanic feature at 18.56 deg N, 61.81 deg E.

name: Artemis III Candidate Region: Haworth (Region)
notes: Candidate landing region, not a pinpoint landing point. Approximate region centroid at 86.76 deg S, 4.85 deg W (-4.85 deg E). Included in NASA updated candidate landing shortlist (October 2024) and Lunar Surface Data Book.

name: Artemis III Candidate Region: Malapert Massif (Region)
notes: Candidate landing region, not a pinpoint landing point. Approximate region centroid at 85.99 deg S, 357.07 deg E (-2.93 deg E in -180..180 system). High Earth visibility and long periods of direct line-of-sight communication.

name: Artemis III Candidate Region: Mons Mouton Plateau (Region)
notes: Candidate landing region, not a pinpoint landing point. Approximate region centroid on the broad flat plateau of Mons Mouton (~84.80 deg S, 28.50 deg E). Selected in NASA refined Artemis III shortlist.

name: Artemis III Candidate Region: Nobile Rim 1 (Region)
notes: Candidate landing region, not a pinpoint landing point. Region centroid along the high-standing northern rim of Nobile impact crater (~84.50 deg S, 54.00 deg E). Scientifically rich volatile prospecting zone.

name: Artemis III Candidate Region: de Gerlache Rim 2 (Region)
notes: Candidate landing region, not a pinpoint landing point. Approximate centroid on the eastern rim of de Gerlache crater (~88.30 deg S, 70.00 deg W / -70.00 deg E). Retained in NASA refined October 2024 shortlist.

name: Artemis III Candidate Region: Connecting Ridge (Region)
notes: Candidate landing region, not a pinpoint landing point. Situated along the prominent topographic ridge connecting Shackleton and de Gerlache craters (~89.47 deg S, 222.60 deg E / -137.40 deg E).

name: Shackleton Crater Rim
notes: Key lunar south-pole science feature (21 km diameter). Rim peaks experience over 80-90 percent illumination throughout the lunar year, while crater interior is in permanent shadow harboring deep water ice. Exact South Pole (90.0 deg S) lies on its rim.

name: Connecting Ridge (Science Region)
notes: South-pole science feature and candidate region. High-standing geographic ridge connecting Shackleton and de Gerlache craters. Representative site CR-1 evaluated for sustained solar illumination and rover traverse corridors. Coordinates: 89.468 deg S, 222.60 deg E (-137.40 deg E in -180..180 system).

name: de Gerlache Crater Rim 1 (Science Region)
notes: South-pole science feature and candidate region. Elevated rim of de Gerlache crater (32.7 km diameter) centered at 88.48 deg S, 88.34 deg W. Evaluated in NASA Artemis Campaign Development Data Book (Site R11: 88.6834 deg S, 67.9321 deg W / -67.932 deg E) for high illumination and science operations.
